_why: published_model_name is the opt-in for the auction census's second exact-identity channel. A card declares the string the maker or auction house actually prints as the MODEL name. Exact normalised equality means it can only ever catch the bare name — 'Day-Date II' and 'Day-Date 40' normalise differently and cannot be swept in. The failure mode that is NOT protected by that is a bare name that is itself a FAMILY: 'Day-Date' is a Rolex line spanning refs 1803 to 2286 and roughly $10k to $2M, so declaring it on one card would sweep a whole line into a single reference. That is a near-miss dressed as an identity. These are the known lines of the houses in this register. Adding one is a one-line commit; removing one is a one-line commit and will fail the test until every card that used it is fixed.
